analysis: What changed vs the 7:00 AM brief: the tape faded from a tech-led open to near-flat by late morning (S&P +0.15%, Nasdaq -0.02%, Dow +0.26% at 10:17 a.m. ET), and the morning's big losers all pared their drops — GE Vernova from -5.5% to about -3.6%, Seagate from -6.5% to about -0.8%, Robinhood from -8.4% to about -2.8%. That is dip-buying into a Fed day, not a reversal of the strict-grading rule: the winners are still the same names (memory, Vertiv, GE HealthCare) and the only new money is rotating into health care, now the day's best sector. Breadth stayed narrow — just 4 of 11 sectors higher, equal-weight S&P down on the day — so the index gains rest on a handful of chip names plus health care. Signal: the memory bid extended rather than faded (SK Hynix ADR past +10%, Micron near +5%, semicap tools up), and GE HealthCare's beat-and-raise shows good quarters can still be bought when the bar isn't already priced in. Noise: single-stock intraday percentages keep moving fast (GEV and STX both moved several points off their early lows), and the oil premium still rests on the unconfirmed refinery-strike claim. The EIA inventory report was due 10:30 a.m. ET; no outcome surfaced in the sources checked for this brief, so the API draw (2.03M barrels) vs the Reuters poll (a small build) setup still stands until confirmed. Everything now funnels into 2:00 p.m. ET and the two cloud prints after the close.
disclaimer: Not financial advice — for informational purposes only.

headlines.headline: The open's tech lead faded to near-flat by late morning: S&P 500 +0.15% at 7,734.00, Nasdaq -0.02% at 26,471.86, Dow +0.26% at 52,514.31 as of 10:17 a.m. ET, with only 4 of 11 sectors higher — health care (+0.70%) led, real estate (-1.14%) lagged, and the equal-weight S&P 500 was down on the day.
headlines.why_it_matters: A flat tape with narrow breadth into a Fed decision — the market is holding position, not adding risk, ahead of 2:00 p.m. ET.

headlines.headline: Memory extends its lead: SK Hynix's US-listed shares +10% (over +11% in a mid-morning sweep) after record Q3 results and a large capital-return package, Micron +4.7-5.0%, and semicap tools (Lam +3.6%, Applied +3.2%, KLA +2.7%) rising with it; Samsung rose 9% in Seoul.
headlines.why_it_matters: The one bid that strengthened after the open rather than fading — fresh demand evidence keeps pulling money into memory and its suppliers.

headlines.headline: Vertiv holds its pop at +12-14% in morning trading after its Q3 blowout (EPS $2.21 vs $1.82 expected, revenue +60.8% to $4.31B, Q4 guide above consensus, orders more than doubled).
headlines.why_it_matters: Cooling/power is still the AI-infrastructure winner being rewarded after the open — the exception to the morning's sell-the-beat pattern.

headlines.headline: The morning's big losers pared their drops: GE Vernova recovered to about -3.6% (from -5.5% early) despite its beat, raise, and $9B Trench deal; Seagate recovered to about -0.8% (from -6.5%) despite its fiscal Q1 beat; Robinhood recovered to about -2.8% (from -8.4%) after its Q3 miss on crypto weakness.
headlines.why_it_matters: Dip-buying softened the sell-the-beat message but didn't reverse it — all three are still down on good-or-bad prints, so tonight's cloud bar stays high.

headlines.headline: Boston Scientific fell 7.7% after a long-expected full-year guidance cut, citing operational disruptions and business impacts from a late-August cyberattack.
headlines.why_it_matters: A guidance cut with a concrete cause (cyberattack disruption) — the market is punishing lowered outlooks harder than backward-looking misses.

headlines.headline: GE HealthCare gained 7.7% after beating Q3 projections and raising annual guidance, now expecting 4% organic revenue growth for the year, up from 3-4% previously.
headlines.why_it_matters: The mirror image of Boston Scientific — a beat plus a raise still gets bought when the bar isn't already priced in, and it flipped health care to the day's best sector.

headlines.headline: Wendy's jumped about 14% to $7.03 after Trian Fund Management submitted an all-cash offer to acquire it for $7.35 a share, valuing the chain at $1.4 billion — a 20% premium to Tuesday's close.
headlines.why_it_matters: A takeover premium in a beaten-down consumer name — deal news, not sector strength, is doing the lifting here.

headlines.headline: Megacaps mixed into tonight's prints (mid-morning snapshot): Alphabet +1.3%, Amazon +0.2%, Nvidia +0.04%, Microsoft -0.3%, Apple -0.6%, Meta -0.8%, Tesla -2.1%. Options traders expect post-earnings moves of 5.09% for Microsoft and 5.99% for Alphabet; consensus is Microsoft EPS $4.73 on ~$90.6B revenue (Azure growth near 45%) and Alphabet EPS $3.03 on ~$127.9B revenue (Google Cloud near $29.15B).
headlines.why_it_matters: No consensus direction into the close — the split tape plus 5-6% implied swings says the cloud growth and capex numbers matter more than headline EPS.

headlines.headline: The Fed decision lands at 2:00 p.m. ET with Chair Warsh's press conference at 2:30 p.m. ET; a hold at 3.75-4.00% is priced at roughly 90-93%, while December hike odds sit at 86% per CME FedWatch.
headlines.why_it_matters: A hold is priced in, so December guidance is the trade — firming December odds plus oil above $101 keep the hawkish-steer risk live.

headlines.headline: Oil holds its premium: WTI ~$101.91 (+2.0%) and Brent ~$115.90 (+1.8%) after Yemen's Houthis said they hit Saudi Arabia's Ras Tanura refinery (550,000 barrels/day) with a missile; Saudi authorities have not confirmed the strike or any damage. API data showed a 2.03M-barrel draw vs a Reuters poll expecting a small build.
headlines.why_it_matters: A supply-risk premium is back in crude hours before the Fed decision — single-source, unconfirmed on the strike itself, so treat the geopolitical leg as fragile even as the price move is real.

market_snapshot.breadth_notes: Morning session Wed Oct 28 (as of ~10:17 a.m. ET): 4 of 11 sectors higher, health care +0.70% best, real estate -1.14% worst; equal-weight S&P 500 down on the day, so breadth stayed narrow beneath the index gains. Prior regular session (Tue Oct 27): S&P 500 +0.60% to 7,722.60, Nasdaq +1.18% to 26,477.81, Dow +0.03% to 52,377.57.
market_snapshot.notes: Wed Oct 28, 8:00 AM PT — ~90 minutes into the 6:30 AM PT open. Index/sector levels per Pulsafi 10:17 a.m. ET read; single-stock moves per Barron's movers and Finnhub current prices. 10-year 5.00% is the Pulsafi intraday read, -1 bp vs the 7 AM brief's 5.01%.

usac.why_it_matters: No fresh USAC company news this morning. The Q3 distribution of $0.525 per common unit ($2.10 annualized) pays Nov 6 to holders of record Oct 26. Q3 earnings are scheduled before the open Tue Nov 3 per the company's own release (11 a.m. ET call), though MarketBeat's calendar lists Nov 4 — the company date governs unless USAC updates it. Last reported quarter (Q2, Aug 4): EPS $0.31 beat the $0.28 consensus, revenue $342.15M vs $340.49M expected. WTI holding above $101 on the Saudi refinery headlines keeps the energy backdrop supportive with no company-specific catalyst.
